title: English colonization of North America
summary: After failed attempts at Roanoke and Newfoundland, the Virginia Company of London founded Jamestown on the James River in 1607, England's first permanent settlement in North America. Disease, hunger and conflict with the Powhatan confederacy marked its first years, until tobacco became a cash crop. In 1619 Virginia held the first representative assembly in what is now the United States, and the first documented Africans were forcibly brought there to work. English colonies spread along the coast; in 1776 thirteen of them declared independence from Britain.

uncertainty.note: Exact calendar years for the founding of Jamestown (1607) and the Declaration of Independence (1776).

as_recorded.value: In 1607, 104 English men and boys arrived in North America to start a settlement. On May 13 they picked Jamestown, Virginia for their settlement
England established its first permanent North American settlement, Jamestown, in 1607
By issuing the Declaration of Independence, adopted by the Continental Congress on July 4, 1776, the 13 American colonies severed their political connections to Great Britain

importance.justification: Planted the English-speaking settler society, representative assemblies and slavery from which the United States grew (R3 D3 T3 L3).

audience_note: Mentions the forced transport of enslaved Africans and conflict with Native peoples.

related.because: Tensions over British imperial administration, taxation, and colonial self-governance culminated directly in the American Revolutionary War.
